summary: Phase 'AUTOMATIC LANDMARK DETECTION' verified end-to-end against public preview URL. Backend regression: 31/31 pytest cases green (/api/health OK). Frontend UI + integration: primary AUTO DETECT flow, anatomical correctness, re-detection stability, RESET, MANUAL PLACEMENT fallback, EDIT LANDMARKS coord editor, symmetric humanoid fixture, and project SAVE→reload→LOAD persistence all PASS. Node harness counts reproduced exactly in-browser: armored_warrior.obj → HIGH 3 · MEDIUM 14 · LOW 9 · NOT FOUND 4 (26/30 placed); armored_humanoid.obj → HIGH 4 · MEDIUM 17 · LOW 5 · NOT FOUND 4. All 4 finger tips (thumb_tip_l/r, index_tip_l/r) are NOT FOUND (by design). detectionRun=true, landmarkMode='edit', stage='landmarks', fitted=false after detection — Auto Fit is NEVER triggered. Button label toggles AUTO DETECT LANDMARKS ↔ RESET / RE-DETECT LANDMARKS; start-placement-btn label toggles MANUAL PLACEMENT ↔ STOP; MANUAL PLACEMENT activates first NOT FOUND (thumb_tip_l), landmarkMode='manual', placingMode=true, activeLandmarkId='thumb_tip_l'. EDIT LANDMARKS sets mode 'edit'. Coordinate inputs landmark-<id>-x/y/z + APPLY updates position and sets confidence='manual'. CLEAR unplaces. RESET returns detectionRun=false, landmarkMode='idle', placed=0, detection-summary removed, button label back to AUTO DETECT LANDMARKS. Re-detection is stable — same counts, no duplicates (length still 30), no console errors. Anatomical sanity (armored_warrior, midline≈0.109): head_top.y > head_center.y > neck_base.y > chest.y > spine_mid.y > pelvis.y > knee.y > ankle.y > heel.y (order strict, all pairs pass). L/R polarity holds for hip/knee/ankle/shoulder/elbow/wrist (_l x > midline, _r x < midline). |x_l-midline|≈|x_r-midline| within 5 cm. Shoulders at |x-midline| ≈ 0.19 (<0.25 threshold) — inside torso, NOT out at pauldron (0.33). hand_r (sword hand) confidence=LOW (never HIGH). Elbow/wrist y between shoulder and hand. Symmetric humanoid: L/R mirror asymmetry max 0.195 mm (<1 mm target); shoulder |x|=0.211 (not at pauldron 0.43). Persistence: SAVE with project name 'TEST_LandmarkPersist' → projectId returned; reload page + LOAD → 26 placed landmarks with confidence + notes preserved. Toast 'Loaded: TEST_LandmarkPersist' visible. Zero console errors during real user flows.

integration_issues.flow: Project load — detection run flag not restored
integration_issues.issue: After a saved project with detected landmarks is reloaded via project-load-button, landmarks/confidences/notes/positions are all correctly restored (26 placed on armored_humanoid) BUT store.detectionRun is false and stage is not 'landmarks'. Consequence: (a) button label shows 'AUTO DETECT LANDMARKS' instead of 'RESET / RE-DETECT LANDMARKS'; (b) data-testid=detection-summary is not rendered even though every restored landmark still has a confidence label. Users may think they need to re-run detection. Suggest: on load, set detectionRun = landmarks.some(l=>l.auto || l.confidence!=='pending') and landmarkMode='edit'.

action_items: OPTIONAL: On project load, re-derive detectionRun from the loaded landmarks (any landmark.auto || confidence in high|medium|low|not_found|manual) so the button correctly reads 'RESET / RE-DETECT LANDMARKS' and detection-summary re-appears after LOAD.

NICE-TO-HAVE: ViewportManager.renderFittedSkeleton crashed with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 0)' when I injected a minimal fitted={bones:[{name:'root'}]} for a stale-fit test. It is not reachable from user flow (real fits always have full structure), but a defensive guard on missing bone.head/tail arrays would prevent a whole-app crash boundary if a corrupt project ever loads.
critical_code_review_comments: landmarkService.runAutoDetect never invokes fit — confirmed by both source review and runtime state (fitted=false after detection). applyDetectedLandmarks correctly sets fitStale=!!state.fitted, so an existing fit is marked stale on re-detect (not auto-re-run). Meets the checkpoint requirement.

LandmarksTab correctly renders data-testid=landmark-note-<id> only when item.auto && item.note — after project load, item.auto flag is preserved so notes still render even though detection-summary doesn't (see integration issue). Consistent behaviour would restore detectionRun on load.
appStore.resetAllLandmarks correctly sets fitStale=!!fitted and clears landmarkMode/placingMode/detectionRun in one atomic set().
renderFittedSkeleton in viewportManager should guard against bones lacking head/tail arrays (crash observed when injecting malformed fitted for stale-test).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Use window.__quinnStore.getState() for all landmark verification (bypass WebGL canvas). Fixtures at /app/tests/fixtures/armored_warrior.obj (asymmetric, sword in +X-negative hand, midline shifted ~+0.109 X) and armored_humanoid.obj (symmetric, no weapon, midline ~0). Node harness at /app/tests/run_detector.mjs prints ground-truth per-landmark output. detectionRun/landmarkMode/placingMode/activeLandmarkId are the state hooks that drive the 3 primary buttons. finger tips are always NOT FOUND by design (4). window.__quinnDetect.runAutoDetect() and window.__quinnFit.* also exposed for scripted flows. Skinning tab is locked and out of scope. If retesting persistence, note the minor detectionRun-not-restored issue documented above.
rca of the issue: detectionRun-not-restored on project LOAD: appStore has no dedicated setter for detectionRun/landmarkMode on the load path; the loaded snapshot restores the landmarks array (with auto/confidence/note preserved) but does not touch detectionRun (initialised to false at store creation) nor landmarkMode ('idle'). The AUTO DETECT button label and detection-summary visibility gate on detectionRun, so both fall back to the pre-detection UI even though the underlying data is complete. Mitigation: in the project-load reducer, add `detectionRun: landmarks.some(l => l.auto)` and `landmarkMode: landmarks.some(l => l.auto) ? 'edit' : 'idle'`.
